Understand the example before you adapt it

Follow the source

Each page links to its English source video and explains the question, inputs, analytical approach and outputs described there.

Know the scope

The selected videos demonstrate specific spatial analyses. Read each page alongside its source to understand the data, analytical scope and assumptions.

Keep the method reviewable

Check your own data, parameters and assumptions before adapting an example. A demonstrated result is not a verified outcome for a new location.

Frequently asked questions

How are the examples organized?+

Each of the seven selected videos has one card and one detail page. Analytical tasks from the same video stay together on that page.

What will I find on each page?+

A description of the spatial question, the inputs and method described in the source, the outputs to inspect, review points and the original video.

Can I use the same approach with my own data?+

Use the example to frame the question, then review your data, supported operations, parameters and validation needs. A published example does not guarantee the same result for a different location or dataset.

Bring your next spatial question.

Explore an example, review its method, and start with the data and context your own question needs.
